spans.claim: Norman Storm saw Leila emerge from the Leicester Building
spans.anchor: Leila was going to the city and to this portion of it

spans.claim: Leila died from a blow to the head with a golf club driver
spans.anchor: the rounded knob, and to the sinister clot of red upon it
spans.span: The blow had been delivered with the rounded knob, and to the sinister clot of red upon it there adhered a single golden hair which glinted accusingly in the light.

spans.claim: Storm destroyed the handkerchief stained with Leila's blood
spans.anchor: the handkerchief was a mere wisp
spans.span: The flakes were dropping now like sifting, gray-white down, and the handkerchief was a mere wisp.

spans.claim: Storm planned to conceal the murder as an accident
spans.anchor: Mrs. Storm’s death was due to a fracture of the right temporal caused by a fall
spans.span: As my colleague, Doctor Carr, had already surmised, Mrs. Storm's death was due to a fracture of the right temporal caused by a fall while suffering an attack of _petit mal_.

spans.claim: Jack Horton disappeared with a large sum of money
spans.anchor: John M. Horton, pay clerk for the Mid-Eastern Consolidated Coal Corporation, disappeared
spans.span: John M. Horton, pay clerk for the Mid-Eastern Consolidated Coal Corporation, disappeared on the sixth inst.

spans.claim: Horton was murdered by a blow to the head
spans.anchor: Jack Horton was found murdered with his head bashed in

spans.claim: The black bag with money and pistol was found at Grand Central Station
spans.anchor: The bag with poor old Jack’s hat and a pistol and a lot of old newspapers inside was discovered
spans.span: The bag with poor old Jack's hat and a pistol and a lot of old newspapers inside was discovered in the parcel-checking room of the Grand Central Station.

spans.claim: Newspapers in the bag had outer sheets missing with Storm’s apartment number
spans.anchor: the outer sheets had been removed because they bore the name of the person to whom they had been consigned
spans.span: Because those papers weren't bought haphazard at a news-stand; they'd been delivered from day to day by a regular vendor, and the outer sheets had been removed because they bore the name of the person to whom they had been consigned.

spans.claim: Storm was swindled by Maurice du Chainat
spans.anchor: He had you down for sixty thousand, and as all the other items on the list were verified
spans.span: He had you down for sixty thousand, and as all the other items on the list were verified by the victims themselves I naturally concluded that his plans had gone through in your case.

spans.claim: George Holworthy suspects Storm’s guilt
spans.anchor: George started back from the table, both hands clutching at the meager hair on his temples
spans.span: As the monstrous, almost unbelievable fact was borne in upon him, George started back from the table, both hands clutching at the meager hair on his temples.

spans.claim: Storm killed Leila out of jealousy and rage
spans.anchor: Storm struck, and the small, colorless face with its tantalizing, disdainful curl of the lips vanished

spans.claim: Storm killed Horton to get the money
spans.anchor: Storm’s hand closed over the head of the heavy cane
spans.span: As Horton crossed the threshold Storm's hand closed over the head of the heavy cane, and he drew it out of the stand.

spans.claim: Storm disposed of Horton’s body by throwing it over a wall
spans.anchor: heave the body over the wall——Then a swift thought brought beads of sweat out upon his brow

spans.claim: Storm hid the money in a valise in his apartment
spans.anchor: He had taken the money and stored it in a valise beneath the bed

spans.claim: George Holworthy finds newspapers with Storm’s apartment number in Storm’s trunk
spans.anchor: On a sudden impulse George picked up the desk blotter and unwrapped it
spans.span: On a sudden impulse George picked up the desk blotter and unwrapped it.

spans.claim: Storm’s golf clubs were found in the den
spans.anchor: There lay the golf sticks just as he had supposed
spans.span: There lay the golf sticks just as he had supposed; and gathering them up he left the den, closing the door behind him, and as he entered the other's eyes traveled to his burden, and a sound very like an oath escaped his lips.

spans.claim: Storm planned to isolate George on the fishing trip to prevent discovery
spans.anchor: I want to be just alone with you
spans.span: I don't even want to have a guide fussing around; I want to be just alone with you.

spans.claim: George calls the police to arrest Storm
spans.anchor: George lifted the receiver
spans.span: Slowly, determinedly, George lifted the receiver.

spans.claim: Storm confesses under pressure
spans.anchor: You killed her with—this!
spans.span: You killed her with-this!" George suddenly produced the driver, and Storm shrank away in horror.

spans.claim: Storm is arrested
spans.anchor: The scream of an approaching siren cut the stillness
